paragraphs: It is Saturday, and Leo has his swim lesson. He has a funny yellow swimsuit with green fish on it. Mia is at the pool, too. The water is blue and cold. "Come on, Leo!" she says. But Leo sits on the floor. "My ear hurts," he says. Then he starts to cry. "I can't swim today," he says.

Mom takes Leo to the doctor. The doctor looks in his ear with a small lamp. "You have an earache," she says. "You are not very ill, but you can't swim for three days." Leo is sad. The doctor is kind and she smiles at him. "What can I do?" he asks. "You can walk, run, and skip," says the doctor. "I can skip!" says Leo. He smiles again.

On Sunday, Leo skips in the garden, and Mia comes. "How is your ear?" asks Mia. "It's fine now," says Leo. "I can't swim, but I can skip." "I'm afraid of the dentist," says Mia. "I go on Monday, and I cry there." "Be brave," says Leo. "I cry, too, but I get a balloon." Mia laughs. The sun is hot, and the children are happy.
